html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 6. The level opens with guided mode on this chapter: the tags to make, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and five results it ticks while you run — a case stops on the mark, a case is packed, the level completes, every bottle right, under par.

Sixteen bottles. The broken ones go into the scrap bin as before; every other bottle is filled and then packed: the belt ends in the case packer of step 12 (chapter 29), and a case lane on a VFD runs beside it. Four bottles to a case, and when the hopper is empty whatever is left in the infeed goes out as a part case. Par 140 s.

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
A good, filled bottle packed into a case+100
A broken bottle in the scrap bin+100
A broken or short-filled bottle packed into a case−50
A whole bottle in the scrap bin−50
Bottles dropped by the packer with no case under the head (each)−50
An empty case shipped at Case_Out−25
What happensPoints
Complete under par (140 s)+200

The level is complete when the hopper is empty, no bottle is left on the belt or in the packer’s infeed, and every packed case has reached Case_Out. Three stars: no mistakes and under par.

How to pass it, step by step

1. Start from Level 5. Run circuit, release one bottle at a time to the filler, latch the gantry into a class

2. One diverter only. Diverter 1 takes broken bottles into the scrap bin. A whole bottle is not pushed: it

3. Run the case lane. Case_Run while no empty case is under the head:

4. Two speeds and a latch. 60 Hz normally; 15 Hz from the slow-down eye until an empty case is on the

5. Scale to the analog output. SCP(Case_Hz,0,60,0,10000,Case_Speed_Ref). Writing 60 or 15

6. Drop only on a stopped, empty case. Group ready, case in place, case not full,

7. Finish the batch. Count the releases with a CTU preset 16; when it is done and the last bottle has left

Run, release, leaving the filler, gantry, class word and fill

Level 5’s first 23 rungs, word for word.

Diverter 1: broken bottles to the scrap bin

The last diverter’s "otherwise" rung passes nothing on: a whole bottle simply runs to the end of the belt.

The case lane: run, creep, speed and scaling

The same seven rungs as the bottle line’s step 12, with Run in place of Line_Run. The speed comes first, or the case cannot move: 60 Hz while not creeping, SCP out to the 0-10 V reference and back from the drive’s output frequency. Then the lane runs while no empty case is on the mark, a latched creep from the slow-down eye, and 15 Hz while creeping.

Counting the batch and packing

The CTU counts rising edges of Infeed_Release; at 16 the hopper is empty. The TON starts when the last bottle has left the filler (Busy off) and gives it 15 s to run down the belt — the belt is 780 px long at 80 px/s, so about 5 s is needed; 15 s is generous and costs nothing, because the timer only starts at the very end. The PACK rung drops on a full group as usual, or, once the tail timer is done, on whatever is left in the infeed (GRT(Infeed_Count,0)): the packer takes up to four, so the part case gets the last one, two or three.

Watch for: the level that never ends

Sixteen bottles minus the broken ones is rarely a multiple of four. Pack only on Group_Ready and the last bottles wait in the infeed for a group that never comes: the hopper is empty, the belt is clear, and the level does not complete. A real line has the same problem at the end of every batch — the last case is a part case, and someone has to decide to send it.

Run it

Load your program, Run mode, Start. Watch the first case come in fast, slow at the eye, stop on the mark; bottles collect in the infeed (the count on the packer’s table), and the fourth starts the head. The Simulator Log shows every pack and every scrap-bin push, with points. A run on 16 of 16 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 112 s against a par of 140 s: 1800 points and three stars.

Try It

Go for a faster time: the line stops at the filler for every fill, so the packer is never the bottleneck — or is it? Set the case feeder’s interval to 8 s and find out. Then pack six to a case (the packer’s Bottles per case, and the CTU and part-case logic still work unchanged).

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in. Stop_PB is a plain button here; E_Stop is 1 while healthy

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt runs unless the filler is holding it
rungs.words: When Run is on and Hold is off, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Hold) Examine If Open asks: true when Hold is off.
  3. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2

pred.q: Run is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Run is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: RELEASE one bottle when the stretch from the hopper to the filler is clear (Busy off). Downstream can hold as many as you like
rungs.words: When Run is on, Busy is off, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false), latches Busy on and unlatches Filled.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Busy is off.
  3. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  4. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Busy) Output Latch does: latches Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Filled) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Filled. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: LEAVING THE FILLER: when the eye under the nozzle has seen the bottle and then lost it, the bottle is on its way to the diverters

pred.q: PE_Fill is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: AtFill latches on.

rungs.words: When PE_Fill (Presence eye under the fill nozzle) is on, the rung latches AtFill on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Fill is on.
  2. OTL(AtFill) Output Latch does: latches AtFill on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: AtFill stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: Load its class into zone 1’s queue, free the front of the line for the next bottle, and forget what the gantry saw
rungs.words: When AtFill is on, PE_Fill (Presence eye under the fill nozzle) is off and this is the first scan of it, the rung loads Class (The bottle in the gantry: bit 0 S, 1 M, 2 L, 3 broken, 4 red, 5 blue, 6 green) into the queue Q1[0] (Zone 1 queue: classes of the bottles between the filler and diverter 1), unlatches Busy, unlatches AtFill, unlatches Is_Low, unlatches Is_Mid, unlatches Is_High, unlatches Is_Broken, unlatches Is_R, unlatches Is_B and unlatches Is_G.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(AtFill) Examine If Closed asks: true when AtFill is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Fill is off.
  3. ONS(Leave_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Leave_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. A branch of 10 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFL(Class,Q1[0],Q1_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Class into the queue Q1[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Busy. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(AtFill) Output Unlatch does: unlatches AtFill. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Is_Low) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Low. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Is_Mid) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Mid. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Is_High) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_High. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 7
    1. OTU(Is_Broken) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Broken. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 8
    1. OTU(Is_R) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_R. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 9
    1. OTU(Is_B) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_B. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 10
    1. OTU(Is_G) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_G. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. LES(Fill_Level,97) Less Than asks: true when Fill_Level is less than 97.
  3. OTE(Fill_Valve) Output Energize does: turns Fill_Valve on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 22

pred.q: Hold is off and Fill_Level is 96. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Filled is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Hold).

rungs.words: When Hold is on and Fill_Level (Fill of the bottle under the nozzle, 0-100 % of its label) is at least 97, the rung latches Filled on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. GEQ(Fill_Level,97) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Fill_Level is at least 97.
  3. OTL(Filled) Output Latch does: latches Filled on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Filled stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: DIVERTER 1 (Broken bin): a bottle arrives at its eye; the head of zone 1’s queue is that bottle’s class
rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Q1[0] (Zone 1 queue: classes of the bottles between the filler and diverter 1) into Cur (The class unloaded from a zone queue at a diverter).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div1 is on.
  2. ONS(D1_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in D1_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFU(Q1[0],Cur,Q1_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Q1[0] into Cur. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 24
rungs.comment: If the class fits this bin, arm the pusher
rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is on, this is the first scan of it and Cur.3 (The class unloaded from a zone queue at a diverter) is on, the rung latches Fire_1 on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div1 is on.
  2. ONS(D1_ONS2) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in D1_ONS2). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. XIC(Cur.3) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cur.3 is on.
  4. OTL(Fire_1) Output Latch does: latches Fire_1 on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fire_1 stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 25
rungs.comment: Push while the bottle is at the eye
rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is on and Fire_1 is on, the rung turns Div1 (Diverter 1 cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div1 is on.
  2. XIC(Fire_1) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire_1 is on.
  3. OTE(Div1) Output Energize does: turns Div1 on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 26
rungs.comment: The bottle has gone: disarm

pred.q: PE_Div1 is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Fire_1 is unlatched.

rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is off, the rung unlatches Fire_1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Div1) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Div1 is off.
  2. OTU(Fire_1) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire_1. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire_1 when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 27
rungs.comment: Otherwise it runs on to the end of the belt
rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is on, this is the first scan of it and Fire_1 is off, the rung does nothing (a placeholder).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div1 is on.
  2. ONS(D1_ONS3) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in D1_ONS3). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. XIO(Fire_1) Examine If Open asks: true when Fire_1 is off.
  4. NOP() No Operation does: does nothing (a placeholder).

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 28
rungs.comment: CASE LANE SPEED first, or the drive has no reference and nothing moves. FAST: 60 Hz while not creeping

pred.q: Case_Creep is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Case_Hz is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIO(Case_Creep).

rungs.words: When Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head) is off, the rung puts 60 into Case_Hz (Case lane speed wanted, Hz).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Case_Creep) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Creep is off.
  2. MOV(60,Case_Hz) Move does: puts 60 into Case_Hz. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 29
rungs.comment: SCALE Hz to the analog output: 0-60 Hz = 0-10 V = 0-10000
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung scales Case_Hz (Case lane speed wanted, Hz) from 0…60 to 0…10000 into Case_Speed_Ref (Case lane drive speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10 V = 0-60 Hz).
rungs.ltr: 1. SCP(Case_Hz,0,60,0,10000,Case_Speed_Ref) Scale with Parameters does: scales Case_Hz from 0…60 to 0…10000 into Case_Speed_Ref.

pats.why: A raw number from a module (counts) is turned into engineering units, or the other way, with a straight line between two points.
pats.think: converting a thermometer’s millimetres of mercury into degrees: two marks on the glass are enough to read every other point.

rungs.head: Rung 30
rungs.comment: READ BACK the drive's output frequency as Hz
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung scales Case_Hz_Fbk (Case lane drive output frequency: 0-10000 = 0-60 Hz) from 0…10000 to 0…60 into Case_Hz_Actual (Case lane drive output frequency read back, Hz).
rungs.ltr: 1. SCP(Case_Hz_Fbk,0,10000,0,60,Case_Hz_Actual) Scale with Parameters does: scales Case_Hz_Fbk from 0…10000 to 0…60 into Case_Hz_Actual.

pats.why: A raw number from a module (counts) is turned into engineering units, or the other way, with a straight line between two points.

rungs.head: Rung 31
rungs.comment: CASE LANE: run while no empty case stands under the head, bringing the next one in or carrying a packed one out
rungs.words: When either (Run is on) or (Group_Ready (The packer infeed holds a case worth) is on) and either (Case_In_Place (A case is centred under the packer head) is off) or (Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is on), the rung turns Case_Run (Case lane drive: run (two-wire)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Group_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Group_Ready is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(Case_In_Place) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_In_Place is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Case_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Full is on.
  3. OTE(Case_Run) Output Energize does: turns Case_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 32
rungs.comment: CREEP from the slow-down eye (latched: the eye only sees the case going past), and while a packed case leaves

pred.q: Case_Slow is on and Case_Full is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Case_Creep latches on.

rungs.words: When either (Case_Slow (Slow-down eye on the case lane, 100 px before the packer head) is on) or (Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is on), the rung latches Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Case_Slow) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Slow is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Case_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Full is on.
  2. OTL(Case_Creep) Output Latch does: latches Case_Creep on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Case_Creep stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 33
rungs.comment: An empty case under the head: stop creeping
rungs.words: When Case_In_Place (A case is centred under the packer head) is on and Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is off, the rung unlatches Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Case_In_Place) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_In_Place is on.
  2. XIO(Case_Full) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Full is off.
  3. OTU(Case_Creep) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Case_Creep. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Case_Creep when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 34
rungs.comment: CREEP: 15 Hz, so the case stops on the mark (from 60 Hz the 0.5 s decel ramp would carry it about 37 px past). The SCALE rung above picks it up on the next scan

pred.q: Case_Creep is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Case_Hz is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Case_Creep).

rungs.words: When Case_Creep (Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head) is on, the rung puts 15 into Case_Hz (Case lane speed wanted, Hz).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Case_Creep) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Creep is on.
  2. MOV(15,Case_Hz) Move does: puts 15 into Case_Hz. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 35
rungs.comment: COUNT the bottles out of the hopper: Released.DN means the hopper is empty
rungs.words: When Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) is on, the rung counts Released (Bottles released from the hopper) up by one (preset 16).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Infeed_Release) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Release is on.
  2. CTU(Released,16,0) Count Up does: counts Released up by one (preset 16). It counts false-to-true transitions of the rung, not scans; .DN is on once the count reaches the preset.

pats.t: A counter: one count per false-to-true.
pats.why: Released counts transitions of the rung, not scans, so a part that sits in front of an eye for a second counts once.
pats.think: a clicker at a door: one click per person coming in, however slowly they walk through.
pats.watch: A counter keeps its count until a RES. If the count should start again at each batch, something has to reset it.

rungs.head: Rung 36
rungs.comment: END OF THE BATCH: once the last bottle has left the filler, give it 15 s to reach the packer

pred.q: Released.DN is on and Busy is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Tail_T times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Released.DN (the done bit of Released: Bottles released from the hopper) is on and Busy is off, the rung runs the timer Tail_T (After the last release: time for the last bottle to reach the packer) toward 15000 ms (15 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Released.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Released.DN is on.
  2. XIO(Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Busy is off.
  3. TON(Tail_T,15000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Tail_T toward 15000 ms (15 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Tail_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 37
rungs.comment: PACK: a full group, or at the end of the batch whatever is left; an empty case on the mark, the lane stopped, the head home
rungs.words: When either (Group_Ready (The packer infeed holds a case worth) is on) or (Tail_T.DN (the done bit of Tail_T: After the last release: time for the last bottle to reach the packer) is on and Infeed_Count (Bottles in the packer infeed) is greater than 0), Case_In_Place (A case is centred under the packer head) is on, Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is off, Case_VFD_Running (Case lane drive output frequency above zero) is off, Packer_Ready (Packer head home, not cycling) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Pack_Drop (Packer: pack up to a case worth from the infeed into the case under the head (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Group_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Group_Ready is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Tail_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tail_T.DN is on.
    2. GRT(Infeed_Count,0) Greater Than asks: true when Infeed_Count is greater than 0.
  2. XIC(Case_In_Place) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_In_Place is on.
  3. XIO(Case_Full) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_Full is off.
  4. XIO(Case_VFD_Running) Examine If Open asks: true when Case_VFD_Running is off.
  5. XIC(Packer_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Packer_Ready is on.
  6. ONS(Drop_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Drop_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  7. OTE(Pack_Drop) Output Energize does: turns Pack_Drop on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 38
rungs.comment: CASES on the toolbar
rungs.words: When Case_Full (The case under the head has been packed) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Case_Count (Shown on the toolbar: cases packed) = Case_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Case_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Case_Full is on.
  2. ONS(Case_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Case_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Case_Count,1,Case_Count) Add does: makes Case_Count = Case_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

Q1.desc: Zone 1 queue: classes of the bottles between the filler and diverter 1

PE_Low.desc: Height beam at 30 px: blocked by every size

PE_Mid.desc: Height beam at 44 px: blocked by M and L

PE_High.desc: Height beam at 52 px: blocked by L only

Crack_Sensor.desc: Crack eye: the bottle in front of it is broken

Fill_Level.desc: Fill of the bottle under the nozzle, 0-100 % of its label

Cur.desc: The class unloaded from a zone queue at a diverter

Case_Creep.desc: Latched from the slow-down eye until an empty case stands under the head

Case_Speed_Ref.desc: Case lane drive speed reference: 0-10000 = 0-10 V = 0-60 Hz

Case_Hz_Fbk.desc: Case lane drive output frequency: 0-10000 = 0-60 Hz

Case_Hz_Actual.desc: Case lane drive output frequency read back, Hz

Group_Ready.desc: The packer infeed holds a case worth

Case_In_Place.desc: A case is centred under the packer head

Case_Full.desc: The case under the head has been packed

Case_Slow.desc: Slow-down eye on the case lane, 100 px before the packer head

Tail_T.desc: After the last release: time for the last bottle to reach the packer

Case_VFD_Running.desc: Case lane drive output frequency above zero

Pack_Drop.desc: Packer: pack up to a case worth from the infeed into the case under the head (rising edge)
